'''Muthusamy Lakshmanan''' (born 25 March 1946) is an Indian [[theoretical physicist]] currently working as Professor of Eminence at the Department of Nonlinear Dynamics of [[Bharathidasan University]]. Presently he is the DST-SERB National Science Chair awarded by the Science and Engineering Research Board, [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]]. He has held several research fellowships which included Raja Ramanna fellowship of the [[Department of Atomic Energy]], [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow|Alexander von Humboldt fellowship]], [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] fellowship, [[Royal Society]] [[Nuffield Foundation]] fellowship, and [[National Academy of Sciences, India|NASI]]-Senior Scientist Platinum Jubilee Fellowship. On 15 August 2021, he was conferred with the Dr. A. P. J Abdul Kalam Award by the [[Government of Tamil Nadu]].

Known for his research on [[nonlinear dynamics]] and for the development of ''Murali-Lakshmanan-Chua (MLC) Circuit'', Lakshmanan is an elected fellow of all three major Indian science academies – [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[Indian National Science Academy]] and [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] – as well as of [[The World Academy of Sciences]]. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to physical sciences in 1989.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link – please select award year to see details}}

== Biography ==
Muthusamy Lakshmanan was born on 25 March 1946 in [[Pollachi]], in the [[Coimbatore district]] of the south Indian state of [[Tamil Nadu]]. He graduated in science from NGM College in Pollachi in 1966 and earned his master's degree in physics (MSc) at [[Madras Christian College]] of the [[University of Madras]] in 1969.<ref name="Bio-Bibliometrics Analysis of Literature Output of Prof. M. Lakshmanan in the Subject of Nonlinear Dynamics">{{Cite web |url=https://apjlis.msu.ac.th/index.php/APJLIS/article/viewFile/85/91 |title=Bio-Bibliometrics Analysis of Literature Output of Prof. M. Lakshmanan in the Subject of Nonlinear Dynamics |date=2012 |publisher=Asia Pacific Journal of Library and Information Science}}</ref> His post-MSc studies in theoretical physics were also at the University of Madras, completed with a first rank in 1970. He joined the university as a research assistant the same year.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae on Bharathidasan University">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bdu.ac.in/centers/non_linear_dynamics/docs/dr_ml.pdf |title=Curriculum Vitae on Bharatidhasan University |date=2017 |publisher=Bharatidasan University}}</ref> Simultaneously, he pursued his doctoral studies, supervised by P. M. Mathews,<ref name="About the Physics Department">{{Cite web |url=https://www.mcc.edu.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=857&Itemid=429 |title=About the Physics Department |date=2017 |publisher=Madras Christian College |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150322180956/http://mcc.edu.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=857&Itemid=429 |archive-date=2015-03-22 }}</ref> to secure a PhD in nonlinear dynamics in 1974.<ref name="About the Physics Department"/>

Taking a sabbatical from university service, he did his post-doctoral studies first at the [[University of Tübingen]] as an [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow|Alexander von Humboldt fellow]] during 1976–77, and then at the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] from 1977 to 1978.<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N92-1094 |title=Indian fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy}}</ref> On his return to India, he rejoined University of Madras at their Post-Graduate Centre at [[Tiruchirapalli]] as a reader of physics, and held this post until 1982 when he moved to the physics department of [[Bharathidasan University]] as a reader. He was promoted as a professor<ref name="M. Lakshmanan">{{Cite web |url=https://globalprofessorrank.com/professors/m-lakshmanan |title=M. Lakshmanan |date=2017 |publisher=Global Professor Rank}}</ref> in 1984, after which he headed the department of physics (1994–2006) as well as the Centre for Nonlinear Dynamics (CNLD) (1992–2006).<ref name="Author profile">{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GEASRPDGXzsC&pg=PA330 |title=Author profile |last1=Muthusamy Lakshmanan |last2=K. Murali |publisher=World Scientific |year=1996 |isbn=978-981-02-2143-0 |pages=330–}}</ref> In between, he served as an honorary professor at [[S.N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences]] from 1989 to 1994.<ref name="Faculty Profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bdu.ac.in/schools/physics/physics/dr_m_lakshmanan.php |title=Faculty profile |date=2017 |publisher=Bharathidasan University}}</ref>

During his university service, Lakshmanan had several stints abroad: at the Institute of Science and Technology of the [[University of Manchester]] during 1979–80 as Royal Society Nuffield Foundation fellow, as a guest scientist at [[Uppsala University]] in 1981, and as a [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] fellow at [[Kyoto University]] from 1984 to 1985.<ref name="Scientometric Portrait of Professor M. Lakshmanan">{{Cite web |url=http://14.139.186.108/jspui/bitstream/123456789/29160/1/2016%20Lakshmanan.pdf |title=Scientometric Portrait of Professor M. Lakshmanan |last=M. Surulinathi, R. Balasubramani |year=2016 |publisher=International Journal of Information Security Science}}</ref> He also filled short-term assignments at 
institutions such as the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (1975 and 1986), [[Utrecht University]] (1975), [[Indian Institute of Science]] (1976), NATO Advanced Study Institute (1980), [[University of Melbourne]] (1980), [[University of Adelaide]] (1980), [[Indian Institute of Technology Madras]] (1982), [[Pondicherry University]] (1988), Centro di cultura scientifica Alessandro Volta (1988), [[Fudan University]] (1989), [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (1990), [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] (as an [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] exchange fellow – 1991), [[Royal Society]] (as an [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] exchange visitor – 1996), [[University of Turku]] (1997), and [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (as an [[Indian National Science Academy|INSA]] exchange visitor – 1996).<ref name="Curriculum Vitae on Bharathidasan University" /> He superannuated from service in 2006. Post-retirement, he was nominated as a professor of eminence by Bharathidasan University and continued his association with the university as a [[Raja Ramanna]] fellow of the Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences (BRNS) of the [[Department of Atomic Energy]] (DAE) during 2006–07. After the expiry of the tenure of the fellowship, the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] selected him as a Ramanna fellow in 2007. In 2011, DAE offered him the Raja Ramanna fellowship for a second term and he continued his research at the university.<ref name="Faculty Profile" />

== Legacy ==
{{Resume-like|section|date=June 2017}}
[[File:Soliton hydro.jpg|thumb|right|[[Soliton]]]]
[[File:Double-compound-pendulum.gif|thumb|right|A [[double pendulum|double rod pendulum]] animation showing [[Chaos theory|chaotic behavior]]]]
Lakshmanan has done extensive research in the field of nonlinear dynamics, especially on [[soliton]]s and [[chaos theory]].<ref name="Scientometric Portrait of Professor M. Lakshmanan" /> One of the first Indian theoretical physicists to use [[differential geometry|differential geometrical methods]] such as [[Painlevé transcendents]] and [[Lie theory]] for studying the [[Integrable system|integrability]] of chaotic systems, he demonstrated ''unsuspected transformations'' and proposed variables for exposing hidden nonlinear structures.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/content/Detail.aspx?AID=170 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> Collaborating with K. Murali and [[Leon O. Chua]], he developed a non-autonomous chaotic circuit, ''Murali—Lakshmanan-Chua (MLC) Circuit''<ref name="An eigenvalue study of the MLC circuit">{{Cite book |chapter=An eigenvalue study of the MLC circuit |date=2002 |publisher=IEEE xplore|doi=10.1109/ICECS.1998.814935 |isbn=0-7803-5008-1 |title=1998 IEEE International Conference on Electronics, Circuits and Systems. Surfing the Waves of Science and Technology (Cat. No.98EX196) |last1=Lindberg |first1=E. |last2=Murali |first2=K. |volume=2 |pages=521–524 |s2cid=54013004 |chapter-url=https://backend.orbit.dtu.dk/ws/files/4364436/Lindberg.pdf }}</ref><ref name="Murali—Lakshmanan-Chua (MLC) Circuit">{{cite book|author1=Muthusamy Lakshmanan|author2=Shanmuganathan Rajaseekar|title=Nonlinear Dynamics: Integrability, Chaos and Patterns|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GOPtCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA171|date=6 December 2012|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-642-55688-3|pages=171–}}</ref> which they detailed in an article, ''Controlling and Synchronization of Chaos in the Simplest Dissipative Non-autonomous Circuit'', published in [[International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos]] in 1995.<ref name="Controlling ans Synchronization of Chaos in the Simplest Dissipative Non-autonomous Circuit">{{Cite journal |last=K. Murali M. Lakshmanan, L.O. Chua |title=Controlling and Synchronization of Chaos in the Simplest Dissipative Non-autonomous Circuit |journal=International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos|volume=05 |issue=2 |pages=563–571 |doi=10.1142/S0218127495000466 |bibcode=1995IJBC....5..563M |year=1995 }}</ref> He studied [[Heisenberg model (quantum)|Heisenberg spin chains]] with respect to its [[solitons]]<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=15 May 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> and elucidated the collision of optical solitons in [[Multi-mode optical fiber|multimode fibres]] and demonstrated the energy sharing between them.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> The body of his work has assisted in the development of applications based on [[ferromagnetism]] and [[nonlinear optics]].<ref name="TWAS Elects Fifty New Members">{{Cite web |url=https://twas.org/article/twas-elects-fifty-new-members |title=TWAS Elects Fifty New Members |date=2009 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles<ref name="On Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=OP7lpFkAAAAJ&hl=en |title=On Google Scholar |date=2017 |publisher=Google Scholar}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}}<ref name="Scientometric Portrait of Professor M. Lakshmanan" /> and the online article repository of Indian Academy of Sciences has listed 256 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Lakshmanan=3AMuthusamy=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> Besides, he has published nine books<ref name="Faculty Profile" /> which include "Nonlinear Dynamics: Integrability, Chaos and Patterns",<ref name="LakshmananRajaseekar2012">{{cite book|author1=Muthusamy Lakshmanan|author2=Shanmuganathan Rajaseekar|title=Nonlinear Dynamics: Integrability, Chaos and Patterns|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GOPtCAAAQBAJ|date=6 December 2012|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-642-55688-3}}</ref> "Chaos in Nonlinear Oscillators: Controlling and Synchronization",<ref name="Lakshmanan1996">{{cite book|author=Muthusamy Lakshmanan|title=Chaos in Nonlinear Oscillators: Controlling and Synchronization|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9rg2nwEACAAJ|year=1996|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-02-2143-0}}</ref> "Symmetries and Rassias|title=Topics in Mathematical Analysis: A Volume Dedicated to the Memory of A.L. Lakshmanan founded the ''Centre for Nonlinear Dynamics'' of Bharathidasan University and served as the head of the centre for almost a decade and half from 1992 to 2006.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He is a member of the editorial board of [[International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos]]<ref name="International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos">{{Cite web |url=http://www.worldscientific.com/page/ijbc/editorial-board |title=International Journal of Bifurcation and Chaos |date=2017 |publisher=World Scientific}}</ref> and has been associated with many other journals such as ''[[Advances in Mathematical Physics]]'', ''Physics News'', [[Journal of Nonlinear Mathematical Physics]], [[Indian Journal of Physics]] and [[Proceedings of the Royal Society|Proceedings of the Royal Society of London A]]. He also served as the guest editor-in-chief of [[Chaos, Solitons and Fractals]] when they published a special issue on solitons in 1995. He has been involved in the organization of the international conferences, workshops and winter schools and is a member of the organizing committee of the 3rd ''International Conference on Symmetries, Differential Equations and Applications'' (SDEA-III) scheduled to be held at [[Istanbul Technical University]] in August 2017.<ref name="SDEA-III">{{Cite web |url=http://sdea3.org/en/COMMITTEES.html |title=SDEA-III |date=2017 |publisher=International Conference on Symmetries, Differential Equations and Applications}}</ref> He delivered the keynote address as the chief guest at the workshop on ''Nonlinear Dynamics and its Applications'' organized by Indian Academy of Sciences and Bharathidasan University in 2003<ref name="Nonlinear Dynamics and its Applications">{{Cite web |url=http://web-japps.ias.ac.in:8080/SEP/Reports/report_lw/21_2005_10.pdf |title=Nonlinear Dynamics and its Applications |date=2003 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> and was the session chair of the ''Physics and Applied Mathematics Researchers' Meet'' (PAAMRM-2015) held at [[Indian Statistical Institute]] in March 2015.<ref name="Programme Schedule">{{Cite web |url=http://www.isical.ac.in/~pamrm2015/Program.pdf |title=Programme Schedule |date=2015 |publisher=Indian Statistical Institute}}</ref> He was also an invited speaker at the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] conference on ''Nonlinear Waves and Coherent Structures (NW08)'' in July 2008, at the international conference on ''Nonlinear Evolution Equations and Dynamical Systems-2009'' in Italy in May 2009, at the Robin Bullough Memorial Meeting of the University of Manchester in June 2009, at the ''Symmetry plus Integrability'' conference in Texas in June 2011, at ''Physcon-2011'' in Spain in September 2011 and at the international conference on ''Frontiers in Mathematics'' at [[Guwahati University]] in March, 2015.<ref name="Proceedings of the International Conference on Frontiers in Mathematics">{{Cite web |url=http://www.gauhati.ac.in/ICFM2015.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Conference on Frontiers in Mathematics |date=2015 |publisher=Guwahati University |work=About the speaker |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709002617/http://www.gauhati.ac.in/ICFM2015.pdf |archive-date=2017-07-09 }}</ref> When the National Academy of Sciences, India organized a national symposium on "New Materials" in 1987, he was among the organizers of the event and he served in the councils of the other two major Indian science academies, at Indian National Science Academy during 2005–07<ref name="Indian fellow" /> and at Indian Academy of Sciences from 2010 to 2012;<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Lakshmanan,_Prof._Muthusamy |title=Fellow profile |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He also was on the [[National Board for Higher Mathematics]] from 1989 to 1992.<ref name="Curriculum Vitae on Bharathidasan University" />

== Awards and honors ==
Lakshmanan received two early career awards in 1980, viz. the Young Scientists Award of the [[University Grants Commission of India]] and the Raman Research Prize of the [[University of Madras]].<ref name="Author profile" /> Four years later, he received the Best University Teacher Award of the [[Government of Tamil Nadu]].<ref name="Faculty Profile" /> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 1989.<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |title=CSIR list of Awardees |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref> The UGC honored him again in 1990 with the Hari Om Trust [[Meghnad Saha]] Award and he received the Tamil Nadu Scientists Award in 1994,<ref name="Proceedings of the International Conference on Frontiers in Mathematics" /> followed by Hari Om Ashram Prerit Shri Hari Vallabhdas Chunilal Shah Research Endowment Prize in 1996.<ref name="Faculty Profile" /> He was selected as a Distinguished Scientist by the [[Indian Science Congress Association]] in 2004 and [[Kurukshetra University]] awarded him the Goyal Prize in Physics the next year.<ref name="Goyal Prize">{{Cite web |url=http://kuk.ac.in/userfiles/file/news/goyal%20prize%202008.pdf |title=Goyal Prize |date=2017 |publisher=Kurukshetra University}}</ref> He received the [[Rameshwar Das Birla|R. D. Birla]] Award Award of the Indian Physics Association in 2014.<ref name="R. D. Birla Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipa1970.org.in/images/Results_Awards.pdf |title=R. D. Birla Award |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Physics Association}}</ref>

Lakshmanan has received seven major research or academic fellowships and five elected fellowships during his career.<ref name="Bio-Bibliometrics Analysis of Literature Output of Prof. M. Lakshmanan in the Subject of Nonlinear Dynamics" /><ref name="Curriculum Vitae on Bharathidasan University" /><ref name="Scientometric Portrait of Professor M. Lakshmanan" /> He has received two research fellowships in the name of [[Raja Ramanna]], from the [[Department of Atomic Energy]] and the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] respectively. The other research fellowships were [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow|Alexander von Humboldt fellowship]] (1976–77), [[Royal Society]] [[Nuffield Foundation]] fellowship (1979–80), [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] fellowship (1984–85), [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] Senior Associate Fellowship (2002–8) and the [[National Academy of Sciences, India|NASI]]-Senior Scientist Platinum Jubilee Fellowship (2016–).<ref name="NASI-Senior Scientist Platinum Jubilee Fellowship">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/NASI-Senior%20Scientist%20Platinum%20Jubilee%20Fellowship%20(2016).htm |title=NASI-Senior Scientist Platinum Jubilee Fellowship |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India}}</ref> The [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] elected him as a fellow in 1989<ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI Year Book 2015 |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India}}</ref> and he became a fellow of the Indian Academy of Sciences<ref name="Fellow profile" /> and the Indian National Science Academy in 1991 and 1992 respectively.<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=15 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 }}</ref> In 2009, The World Academy of Sciences elected him as a fellow.<ref name="TWAS Elects Fifty New Members" /><ref name="TWAS fellow">{{Cite web |url=https://twas.org/member/lakshmanan-muthusamy |title=TWAS fellow |date=2017 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref> The year 2009 brought him another honor by way of [[honoris causa]]
